title_en: Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate v. Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling — embezzlement case
keywords_en: criminal; embezzlement; retrial; basic people's court; Shanghai; natural person; Criminal Law; elements of the crime of embezzlement; illegal possession of public property; risk transfer in futures trading; reversal of judgment; futures trading; shifting losses; state-owned enterprise
full_text_en:
Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate v. Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling — embezzlement

Procuratorial Authority: Huangpu District People's Procuratorate of Shanghai.

Defendant: Dou Peiying, male, 37 years old, manager of the Futures Department of China Nonferrous Metal Materials East China Company. Arrested on April 5, 2002.

Defendant: Xian Xiaoling, female, 36 years old, trader of the Futures Department of Shanghai Metal Materials General Company. Arrested on June 12, 2002.

In the case of embezzlement against defendants Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling, after the Huangpu District People's Procuratorate of Shanghai initiated a public prosecution, the court of first instance, upon trial, held that: Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling, by transferring futures contracts from private accounts into state-owned enterprise accounts when prices were falling, caused the state-owned enterprises to suffer losses from holding positions. This conduct was socially harmful. Since futures prices fluctuate, holders of futures contracts may suffer losses due to price declines or gain profits due to price increases; gains and losses are both normal occurrences in futures trading. Therefore, when Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling transferred futures contracts with falling prices into state-owned enterprise accounts, they merely shifted the risk of futures trading, not actual losses. When futures contracts with falling prices were transferred into state-owned enterprise accounts, before the positions were closed, they only reflected losses from holding positions and did not mean that the state-owned enterprises had already suffered actual losses. It cannot be considered that this conduct constituted illegal possession of state-owned enterprise property. As for the losses subsequently caused to the state-owned enterprises by closing the positions, although there was the factor of others shifting risks, they were mainly caused by the state-owned enterprises' improper holding of futures contracts. Therefore, the conduct of Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling did not satisfy the objective elements of the crime of embezzlement under Article 382 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, which stipulates "embezzling, stealing, defrauding, or using other means to illegally possess public property." Based on this, the court rendered a judgment acquitting Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling. After the judgment became effective, the Shanghai High People's Court, upon review, held that the original judgment was indeed erroneous in the application of law, and thus ordered a retrial. After receiving the order, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, revoked the second-instance ruling and the first-instance judgment, and remanded the case to the Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai for retrial.

Indictment Charges: The defendants, Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling, by taking advantage of their positions, successively transferred two types of futures contracts for plywood and small red beans from private accounts when prices were falling into the accounts of two state-owned enterprises. This not only caused the two state-owned enterprises to incur losses from holding positions on the same day totaling RMB 66,400, but also caused them to suffer losses totaling RMB 513,000 from closing the positions. The conduct of Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling violated Articles 382, 383, and 25 of the Criminal Law, constituting the crime of embezzlement. The Procuratorate requested a judgment according to law.

Defendants Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling raised no objections to the basic facts alleged in the indictment.

Defendant Dou Peiying's Defense: Losses from holding positions fluctuate with the movement of futures prices and are not fixed losses. Although the state-owned enterprises had to add margin for the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction, the added margin still belonged to the state-owned enterprises. If there was a profit the next day, the margin would be returned to the state-owned enterprises. Therefore, if the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction are deemed as public property illegally possessed by others, it becomes impossible to explain the nature of the property of the margin returned after profitable positions. Furthermore, Xian Xiaoling was both the order clerk for her company's account and the account holder of her private account, and had the right to issue instructions for both accounts. The transfer of 300 lots of plywood contracts into the account of Xian Xiaoling's company was an instruction issued to me by Xian Xiaoling, and I had to execute it, but I did require Xian Xiaoling to report to the company's leadership at the time of execution. I had no intent to collude with Xian Xiaoling to shift losses to the state-owned enterprises, much less the criminal purpose of embezzling state-owned enterprise property. Because I was bullish on the price of small red beans, I advised Xian Xiaoling not to close the position, and after a temporary price decline, Xian Xiaoling blamed me; I had no choice but to transfer this small red bean contract to my company's account. This was not a joint intent to shift others' losses to my company. Subsequent facts proved that the price of small red beans rose, and this futures transaction in small red beans generated considerable profit for my company, showing that my judgment was correct.

Defendant Xian Xiaoling's Defense: Our company regulations prohibited order clerks from privately engaging in futures trading. The 300-lot plywood contract was purchased by me for my private account. While I was writing the instruction for these 300 lots on a slip of paper, I was discovered and questioned by the company's deputy general manager, He Wei. Fearing exposure of my private futures trading, I had to falsely claim that I had misheard the instruction and bought them for the company. Therefore, I later had to ask Dou Peiying to record these 300 lots into the company's account, rather than intentionally transferring contracts with falling prices to the state-owned enterprise. As for the 400 lots of small red beans, I instructed to close the position, but Dou Peiying refused to close it for me. Later, the price fell, so naturally he should have bought them; I bear no responsibility or only partial responsibility for this. Moreover, I am not a state functionary and cannot be the subject of the crime of embezzlement; I also have voluntary surrender and should be given a lighter punishment.

The Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts upon trial:

Defendant Dou Peiying, from May 1995, served as the manager of the Futures Department of China Nonferrous Metal Materials East China Company (hereinafter referred to as East China Company). Defendant Xian Xiaoling, from April 1995 to June 1996, served as an order clerk in the Futures Department of Shanghai Metal Materials General Company (hereinafter referred to as Metal Company). The two became acquainted through business dealings. Xian Xiaoling proposed opening a private account in the name of her husband, Zhu Min. Dou Peiying agreed and set up a private account coded 034 in the Futures Department of East China Company for Xian Xiaoling.

On November 1, 1995, defendant Xian Xiaoling telephoned defendant Dou Peiying and instructed him to buy 300 lots of plywood (each lot consisting of 200 sheets, purchase price: RMB 43.7 per sheet) for delivery in November 1995, code 9511, in account 034. After the transaction, the price of plywood declined. To avoid personal losses, Xian Xiaoling, taking advantage of her position as an order clerk, notified Dou Peiying to transfer these 300 lots of contracts into the 001 futures proprietary account of Metal Company. Dou Peiying agreed but required Xian Xiaoling to report to the company's deputy general manager, He Wei. After the market closed that day, Dou Peiying notified the settlement personnel of East China Company to transfer the 300-lot plywood contract originally intended for private account 034 into the 001 proprietary account of Metal Company. Xian Xiaoling falsely told He Wei that these 300 lots were purchased due to mishearing an instruction, and was thus acknowledged by Metal Company and recorded in the company's position summary sheet. The settlement price of plywood on November 1 was RMB 43.06 per sheet. Due to Xian Xiaoling's transfer, the 300-lot plywood contract caused a loss from holding positions of RMB 38,400 for Metal Company on that day. Subsequently, upon He Wei's instructions, Xian Xiaoling closed out these 300 lots by selling, resulting in a total loss of RMB 269,000.

On November 17, 1995, defendant Xian Xiaoling telephoned defendant Dou Peiying and instructed him to buy 400 lots of small red beans (each lot: 2 tons, purchase price: RMB 2,380 per ton) for delivery in December 1995, code 9512, in account 034. After the transaction, the price of small red beans rose. Xian Xiaoling telephoned Dou Peiying to close the position. Dou Peiying believed that the price of small red beans would continue to rise and advised Xian Xiaoling to wait and see; Xian Xiaoling agreed. However, just before the market close that day, the price of small red beans fell. After the market closed, Xian Xiaoling called Dou Peiying, blaming him for not closing the position in time. Dou Peiying insisted that the price would still rise and indicated that if Xian Xiaoling regretted, these 400 lots could be considered as recorded in their company's proprietary account. Xian Xiaoling acquiesced after hearing this. Dou Peiying then telephoned the settlement personnel of East China Company to transfer the contract originally intended for Xian Xiaoling's private account into East China Company's proprietary account coded 018. The settlement price of small red beans on that day was RMB 2,345 per ton. The 400-lot small red bean contract caused a loss from holding positions of RMB 28,000 for East China Company on that day. On November 22 of the same year, Dou Peiying, concerned that the continued decline in the price of small red beans would affect the achievement of that year's profit targets, decided to close out the 400 lots of small red beans. This action caused East China Company a loss of RMB 244,000. After closing the position, the price of small red beans rebounded. Dou Peiying then bought a large quantity and closed out shortly after, generating profits for East China Company.

After the case came to light, defendant Dou Peiying surrendered RMB 440,000, and defendant Xian Xiaoling surrendered RMB 90,000.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence submitted by the Procuratorial Authority and presented and read out in court by the public prosecutor: certificates of the defendants' positions issued by their respective companies; testimony of witnesses Zhu Min and Wang Lin regarding the opening of private account 034 and the futures trading and profit sharing between the two defendants; testimony of witnesses He Wei and Le Wenguang regarding Xian Xiaoling's purchase of 300 lots of plywood for the state-owned enterprise; testimony of witnesses Gu Zhi and Hao Xin regarding the order allocation and settlement in East China Company's Futures Department; documentary evidence including the summary report of transaction slips from East China Company's Futures Department and the position summary sheet of Metal Company; and handwriting expert reports. These pieces of evidence, having been cross-examined in court, are lawful and valid, and are hereby confirmed.

The Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai held:

The conduct of the defendants in this case occurred in November 1995. Article 2 of the "Supplementary Provisions on Punishment of the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery" adopted by the Standing Committee of the Sixth National People's Congress at its 24th Session on January 21, 1988, stipulated the threshold for the crime of embezzlement as follows: "Where the amount of personal embezzlement is less than RMB 2,000, if the circumstances are relatively serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are relatively minor, the offender's unit or competent authority at a higher level shall impose administrative sanctions as appropriate." Paragraph (4) of Article 383 of the Criminal Law of the PRC as amended in 1997 provides: "Where the amount of personal embezzlement is less than RMB 5,000, if the circumstances are relatively serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are relatively minor, the offender's unit or competent authority at a higher level shall impose administrative sanctions as appropriate." Comparing the two, the amended Criminal Law imposes a lighter punishment. Pursuant to the principle of applying the old law but with the lighter punishment under Article 12 of the Criminal Law, the amended Criminal Law shall be applied to this case for conviction and sentencing.

Defendants Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling, as staff members of state-owned enterprises, in conducting futures trading activities for their respective units, took advantage of their positions and used deceptive methods to transfer futures contracts from private accounts into the accounts of state-owned enterprises when prices were falling, causing the state-owned enterprises to suffer losses from holding positions on the day of transfer of RMB 38,400 and RMB 28,000, respectively. This practice of shifting personal losses to state-owned enterprises, although not manifested as direct possession of state-owned property, essentially constitutes a means of possessing state-owned property by using losses of state-owned enterprises to offset personal losses, and is a form of illegal possession. Pursuant to Article 382 of the Criminal Law, the conduct of Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling constitutes the crime of embezzlement, and the charges brought by the Procuratorial Authority are established. The amount of embezzlement in this case shall be calculated based on the settlement price on the day of the transfer of positions by Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling.

According to the "Detailed Rules for Settlement of Suzhou Commodity Exchange" (September 1995), losses from holding positions on the day of a futures contract transaction shall be deducted from the capital settlement account on that day. The daily gains and losses from holding positions during the entire process from contract transaction to closing are both related to and different from the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction. The distinction is that the daily gains and losses from holding positions during the holding period are related to and determined by the daily futures market conditions, and are uncertain; whereas the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction, because they must be deducted from the capital settlement account on that day, become definite and actual losses incurred. The daily gains and losses from holding positions during the holding period are related to the holder's participation in futures trading activities on that day; whereas the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction are the result of capital settlement after the conclusion of futures trading activities on the day of transaction. The two should not be conflated.

Defendants Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling, as staff members of state-owned enterprises, took advantage of their positions and carried out the act of transferring futures contracts from private accounts with falling prices into the accounts of state-owned enterprises. The total loss from holding positions on the day of transfer caused to the state-owned enterprises was RMB 66,400. This is the factual basis for finding that the conduct of the two constitutes the crime of embezzlement. The gains and losses incurred during the period when the transferred futures contracts were held by the state-owned enterprises, although related to the transfer conduct of the two, were not determined by their transfer conduct but by the futures market conditions. Therefore, these gains and losses at that time are not circumstances for determining whether the conduct of the two constitutes a crime but are factors that may be considered in sentencing the two.

Paragraph 1 of Article 25 of the Criminal Law provides: "A joint crime refers to an intentional crime committed by two or more persons jointly." Defendant Xian Xiaoling, in order to make profits, opened account 034 to conduct private futures trading, with profits belonging to herself and losses shifted to state-owned enterprises; defendant Dou Peiying, in order to attract more clients, agreed to set up a private account for Xian Xiaoling and cooperated with her in her premeditated plan to shift losses, each concealing the true facts from their respective units to achieve the criminal purpose of shifting personal futures losses to state-owned enterprises. The two are joint offenders, and they shall bear criminal responsibility respectively based on the roles they played in the joint crime. The illegal gains obtained by the two from shifting losses shall be recovered in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law.

The defenses raised by defendants Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling that the losses from holding positions on the day of transaction were uncertain losses, that they did not occupy company property, and that the small red bean transaction generated profits for the company, thus their conduct does not constitute the crime of embezzlement, much less a joint crime, are not adopted. Furthermore, although Dou Peiying and Xian Xiaoling confessed to their respective criminal facts after being brought to justice, they did not voluntarily surrender and do not meet the statutory conditions for voluntary surrender. Therefore, their defenses seeking a suspended sentence or exemption from criminal punishment on the ground of voluntary surrender are also not adopted. However, based on their confession after being brought to justice and their restitution of illicit gains, a lighter punishment may be imposed as appropriate. Accordingly, the Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai rendered the following judgment on August 21, 2002:

1. Defendant Dou Peiying is convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months.

2. Defendant Xian Xiaoling is convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and nine months.

After the judgment was announced, neither defendant Dou Peiying nor Xian Xiaoling appealed, and the Procuratorial Authority did not file a protest. The first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
